transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (SpruceView — Head of Platform), Markus Feld (SpruceView SRE), Aisha Rahman (SpruceView FinOps)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage breakdown, how to map routes to billing buckets, and a playbook for a pilot to validate cost savings. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs and VPC requirements. Agreed to a short pilot and deliverables.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and route tagging
- Token-level cost and batching impact
- Caching / KV cache behavior and prefix caching
- Dedicated vs hosted routing for critical low-latency routes
- Pilot plan and data handoff

Action items (see metadata list)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Alright uh hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jared Kim from Redwood — I'm the AE on this account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How are we all doing?
[00:05] Lena: Hey Jared, good thanks, thanks for making time.
[00:07] Markus: Hi, Markus here. We got a bit of background deck before this but keen to see the console in action.
[00:11] Aisha: Aisha from FinOps, hi. We're mostly interested in the billing split by route and how we can tie it back to product owners.
[00:16] Priya: Great — we'll focus on the Usage Analytics and per-route dashboards, then show cost decomposition and a playbook for pilot. If we need a deep kernel perf dive we can schedule a separate technical session.

[00:35] Jared: Quick question for context — what's your current serving setup — are you running everything in-house, or on a managed endpoint?
[00:40] Lena: We're hybrid — inference for internal tools is on our infra, but customer-facing chat is hosted on a managed endpoint with autoscaling. We have some routes that are super high-volume, like tile-generation and summarization.
[00:52] Markus: Also we do have some regulatory routes that need data to stay in our VPC.
[00:55] Priya: Got it. That fits the typical mix where Redwood can run hosted for most routes and private/dedicated for the sensitive ones.

[01:15] Priya: Alright I'm going to share my screen — excuse any small noise. We're in the Redwood Console — this is the Usage Analytics overview. At the top you see the token throughput and cost trend.
[01:32] [Speaker 2]: transcript note: small stutter here said "to to"
[01:35] Priya: For SpruceView I've pre-filtered to show the last 7 days and grouped by route. Each row is a logical route that you can tag — e.g., /summarize-article, /customer-chat, /vector-embed. You can add metadata like owner, sensitivity, and billing bucket.

[02:05] Markus: How does the console determine token cost per request? We have variable prompt sizes.
[02:10] Priya: Good question — Redwood shows token-level unit economics derived from the model profile. The console multiplies per-token runtime cost (based on model kernel selection + infra) by actual tokens consumed. There is some approximation for batching and shared KV cache hits — when cache hits occur per-prefix, the accounting will show a lower per-request increment.
[02:35] Lena: That prefix cache thing — we call it a warm cache at our side — will that be reflected? Sometimes our ops team mislabels KV cache as KV cash in docs lol.
[02:44] Priya: (laughs) yes you'll see a separate line item for cache-hit savings. We surface cache hit rate and the estimated tokens saved. Note that the transcription sometimes writes KV as K V so apologies for that in exported CSV.

[03:05] Priya: Here's the route detail page for /summarize-article — on the left timeline you get QPS, 50/95/99 latencies, and tokens. On the right is the cost breakdown: model execution, batching overhead, network egress, and a small per-request control plane charge for hosted mode.
[03:30] Aisha: The per-request control plane charge — can that be disabled for us if we go dedicated?
[03:33] Jared: If you move to Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity, the control plane per-request line is absorbed into the committed rate and your unit cost shifts. We'll show a sample comparison later.

[03:55] [00:04:00] Priya: There's also a route mapping feature — you can group several micro-routes under a single billing route. Useful when your product teams have many tiny endpoints. You can map /v1/chat/* to a single "customer-chat" route.
[04:15] Markus: That's great — our current billing is all lumped per-service and it's hard to map back to PM owners.

[04:35] Priya: I want to point out the batching simulator — under Optimize tab. You can feed the simulator with your request size distribution and it shows how throughput and per-token cost change as we change batch windows. For instance, increasing continuous-batching window from 10ms to 40ms saved ~12% on per-token CPU time in our tests but increased p95 by ~18ms.
[04:57] Lena: Hmm latency tradeoff — for customer-chat we need p95 under 250ms. Do you have expected deltas listed?
[05:05] Priya: Yes, the simulator produces an SLO-impact table. For your summarized routes we saw minimal latency impact because the model comp was more GPU bound; batching improved GPU utilization.

[05:30] [05:30] Jared: On the cost decomposition CSV export we surface both raw tokens and normalized tokens, plus the kernel profile used (e.g., fp16, int8-qat). Some of our customers prefer normalized tokens to compare across model sizes.
[05:48] Markus: You mentioned kernel profile — we have an internal requirement to use quantized variants for cost — is that safe?
[05:54] Priya: We include a quality delta metric in the per-route monitor — you can tie automated regressions to evaluation sets. If a quantized variant has unacceptable regressions we flag it and can automatically rollback.

[06:20] Aisha: On the pilot, we want to validate end-to-end cost delta and confirm attribution to product teams. What's your recommended window?
[06:27] Priya: Typically 2 weeks is enough to capture pattern variability, but if you have weekly batch jobs that spike once a month, go 4 weeks. For billing reconciliation we ask for a sample billing.csv from your current infra — the pilot will produce a mapping and a reconciliation sheet.

[07:00] [07:00] Lena: Action item then: I'll send the traffic mix + billing CSVs.

[07:10] Priya: Thanks. Now quick note on routing policy — Redwood lets you set route-level policy: latency-first, cost-first, or balanced. For a route you can pin to a low-latency model variant (dedicated) and set fallback to a cheaper hosted variant when dedicated pool hits capacity.
[07:30] Markus: So fallback can be automatic? We need strict alerts if fallback happens for regulated routes.
[07:36] Jared: Yes, fallback events are emitted to your audit log and the console shows a per-route fallback metric. For regulated routes we recommend a hard pin to private deployment to avoid fallback.

[07:55] Priya: I'm toggling into the Audit / Security panel — you can see SSO (SAML), RBAC roles, KMS integration for private keys, and per-request audit logs.
[08:10] Lena: Good. We'll want to see the SOC 2 docs and HSM options.

[08:20] Jared: We'll share SOC 2 and our private deployment whitepaper after the call — I'll add that to next steps.

[08:35] [08:35] Priya: Back to the per-route billing — here's a sample reconciliation report. Left column is your routes, middle is the raw cost assigned by Redwood, right column is a suggested product owner mapping which you can edit inline. The reconciliation delta shows where our cost mapping differs from your current ledger. In our test with a similar customer we found a 15% difference, mostly due to unaccounted cache savings and batching.
[09:10] Aisha: That's the kind of number we want to see — if we can reduce customer_chat unit cost by 10% that would be huge.
[09:18] Priya: We also surface attribution to downstream services — e.g., if route X calls embedding and a reranker, we break costs out by subcomponent.

[09:40] Markus: Any limitations on sampling/retention? We need 90 days of logs for our audits.
[09:45] Priya: Console retention defaults to 30 days for high-resolution telemetry but we have extended retention add-ons (60/90/365) you can subscribe to, and for Private deployments your logs can live in your S3 bucket.

[10:05] [10:05] Jared: Let's talk pricing mechanics briefly — hosted is per-token + model premium; Dedicated is committed monthly capacity with lower per-token marginal cost; Private has a platform fee and support. We can run a modeled projection in the pilot.
[10:25] Lena: For Dedicated we have a procurement cycle, so we likely start hosted/pilot then scale to dedicated if the numbers justify it.

[10:40] Priya: Cool. Now I want to show an example anomaly detection: Console flagged an unusual spike in /vector-embed QPS and traced it to a misconfigured crawler. You get an alert and a suggested mitigation: temporary rate limit and a dry-run reroute to a cheaper model for backfills.
[11:05] Markus: Helpful. Does the console also recommend quantization profiles?
[11:10] Priya: Yes, in Optimize we have recommended quantization per-route based on eval thresholds you set.

[11:25] [11:25] Aisha: About the pilot deliverables — can you deliver a single sheet that maps routes to cost buckets and shows projected savings?
[11:33] Jared: Yes — we'll deliver a "route economics workbook" with baseline, pilot results, and projected 12-month savings under different adoption scenarios.

[11:50] Priya: I'll also attach an example playbook — a checklist: tag routes, run baseline export, enable prefix caching, run batching experiments in the sandbox, reconcile costs, and then meet to decide Dedicated path.

[12:10] Lena: Sounds good. Markus — any concerns on infra side?
[12:14] Markus: Mainly the VPC connectivity and that we have deterministic p95 — if pilot shows too many fallbacks or latency spikes it's a blocker.

[12:25] Priya: We'll cap the fallback behavior for those routes and emit immediate alerts. Also, for VPC-enabled private deployments we can pin routing so nothing leaves your VPC.

[12:40] [12:40] Jared: Okay let's do a quick recap and next steps: Jared will provision a sandbox and invite SpruceView by Aug 13; Priya will run the per-route baseline and share a cost/latency table by Aug 17; Lena will send sample traffic mix and billing CSVs by Aug 12; Redwood to send SOC2 & private deploy whitepaper. Pilot kick-off target Aug 24.

[13:10] Aisha: One last quick question — do you have an API to programmatically pull per-route cost?
[13:15] Priya: Yes we expose a Usage API and a Billing Export endpoint. We'll include example curl and python snippets in the sandbox docs.

[13:30] Markus: Great, thanks everyone.
[13:33] Lena: Thanks Jared, Priya.
[13:35] Jared: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and links.
[13:37] [END]
